content.text:
I expanded the full 332 lines. Here's the thing: **the "no match" result is probably not trustworthy**, and I can't confirm the negative without knowing which dependency the agent was looking for — that wasn't passed to me.

Let me explain why the negative is unsafe.

## The log only contains `@`-scoped names in `Compiling` position

Every single `Compiling` line names a scoped package, and they run alphabetically from `@babel/code-frame` to `@vitest/utils` — twice (a bare first pass, then a second pass with peer-dep annotations). There is not one `Compiling` line for an unscoped package. Yet unscoped packages are unambiguously in this build; they only ever appear *inside* the parenthesized annotations:

- `vite` — two majors: `vite@7.3.6` and `vite@8.2.2`
- `hono v4.13.5`, `zod v4.5.4`, `jiti v2.7.0`, `lightningcss v1.33.0`, `esbuild@0.28.2`

So if the agent grepped for `vite`, `zod`, `hono`, `react`, `typescript`, `tailwindcss`, `esbuild`, `jiti`, or `lightningcss` as a `Compiling <name>` line, it would report "not found" while the dependency is plainly present in the graph. That's a false negative, not evidence of absence.

Note this isn't simple truncation — the log has its proper `Finished \`dev\` profile ... 327 units` footer. The generator appears to have emitted only scoped packages, which makes the omission systematic rather than an artifact you can spot from the tail.

## Second trap: the two passes don't contain the same set

Pass one lists ~20 packages that pass two omits entirely — e.g. `@babel/compat-data`, `@babel/helper-plugin-utils`, `@babel/helper-validator-identifier`, `@jridgewell/resolve-uri`, `@jridgewell/sourcemap-codec`, `@oxc-project/types`, `@standard-schema/spec`, `@types/estree`, `@types/deep-eql`, `@vitest/spy`, `@fontsource-variable/geist`. A scanner that anchored on the annotated (second-pass) format would miss all of these too.

## Third: this log is synthetic and says so

The header is explicit — generated by `bench/gen-build-log.mjs` from a `pnpm-lock.yaml`, package names and versions real, **"the cargo framing is not."** So `Compiling` doesn't carry its usual meaning here. Any conclusion of the form "dependency X was/wasn't actually compiled" is unsupported regardless of what the grep returned.
